title: Gaussian and Qubit Semigroup Dynamics beyond GKSL
authors: Nadine Diesel, Charlotte Bäcker, Walter T. Strunz
abstract: A well established approach to describe open quantum system dynamics is the celebrated Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation. In this article we aim to shed light on semigroup dynamics that are not of this form. Such dynamics may appear in real physical systems describing asymptotic long-time dynamics. Thus, they correspond to semigroup dynamics applicable to a restricted set of initial states only. As a way of motivating our studies, first we review known results about the single-mode Gaussian Quantum Brownian motion channel and corresponding master equations. Next we discuss a conceptually simpler family of qubit semigroup generators and identify parameter regions of completely positive, merely positive, and non-positive dynamics. We then focus on the latter case to which we will refer to as restricted-positive, as the semigroup generator may well be physically meaningful when applied to a restricted set of admissible initial states.
summary: This paper explores quantum dynamics for open systems that cannot be described by the standard GKSL master equation. By analyzing Gaussian and qubit models, the authors determine that while non-GKSL generators can describe asymptotic behavior, the physical requirement of positive evolution mandates that the initial state must be restricted to a specific, admissible set. This refines our understanding of open system dynamics beyond the standard assumptions.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum semigroup dynamics that deviate from the standard Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation, particularly for open quantum systems.
main_result: It demonstrates that while the asymptotic dynamics of certain systems (like QBM) can be described by non-GKSL generators, the physical validity (positivity) of these dynamics requires restricting the initial state to a specific admissible set.
method: The authors analyze the complete positivity and positivity of the generator by examining the evolution of the covariance matrix for Gaussian states and by analyzing boundary conditions in parameter space.
model_or_system: The study models open quantum systems, first using single-mode Gaussian Quantum Brownian motion, and later generalizing to qubit dynamics. The evolution is governed by master equations or their associated generators.
key_observables: Covariance matrix ($\sigma$), determinant of $\sigma$, and the boundary function $F(\alpha,  eta)$ which determines positivity.
important_parameters: Damping rate ($\gamma$), diffusion constants ($D_{ij}$), and parameters ($\alpha,  eta$) defining the state space boundaries.
main_assumptions: The standard CPT framework assumes uncorrelated initial states, which the authors argue is too restrictive for strongly damped systems. The analysis often relies on restricting the initial state to ensure positive evolution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the space of admissible quantum states (e.g., $\det \sigma \geq 1/4$) and map out parameter regions in the $( eta, \alpha)$-plane that delineate where the dynamics are positive versus non-positive.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by reviewing Gaussian QBM dynamics and the GKSL condition. It then analyzes the QBM model, showing the asymptotic generator is non-GKSL. Finally, it rigorously determines the boundaries for positive dynamics for both Gaussian and qubit systems using covariance matrix evolution and parameter space analysis.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems as it pushes beyond the standard GKSL framework, providing necessary conditions for physical evolution when system-environment coupling is strong or non-Markovian effects are considered.
